findings.failing_input: A real store tab with data beyond spreadsheet row 100000, e.g. uzoshop-orders-attribution row 100001 containing a valid 2026-05-24 Shopify order. This is realistic at scale because the file comment projects 330k attribution rows and the reader fans out by only three store tabs.
findings.expected: fetchOrdersAttribution() includes every valid row in each <storeId>-orders-attribution tab, including rows after sheet row 100000, then applies date/orderId filtering.
findings.actual: Rows after sheet row 100000 are never fetched because the reader hard-codes `const ranges = STORE_TAB_CONFIG.map(s => `${s.id}-orders-attribution!A2:${lastCol}100000`);`, so revenue/orders beyond that boundary disappear from downstream attribution if this Sheets reader is used.
findings.fix_sketch: Use an open-ended Sheets range such as `${s.id}-orders-attribution!A2:${lastCol}` or page/chunk reads until exhaustion; add a boundary test proving rows at and after sheet row 100001 are included.
findings.regression_test_idea: Mock google.sheets().spreadsheets.values.batchGet and assert requested ranges are open-ended A2:M/A2:N, or simulate a valueRange containing a sentinel order beyond the old cap and verify it is returned.

test_coverage_gaps.description: The existing contract test only exercises parseSource passthrough, whitespace, null/undefined, and a hard-coded writer label list.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: It does not exercise fetchOrdersAttribution row mapping, date filtering, boolean parsing, numeric parsing, missing-tab behavior, or includeLineItems behavior, where output-impacting reader bugs can hide.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Mock Sheets batchGet with one row per store including numeric date, comma-formatted total, TRUE/true booleans, utmId/utmTerm, range outside/inside, and includeLineItems both false and true.

test_coverage_gaps.description: WRITER_EMITS in orderSourceContract.test.ts omits the first-class OrderSource value tiktok-paid even though the source union includes it and Shopify fetcher tests indicate the writer can emit it.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: parseSource still passes tiktok-paid through via the permissive unknown-label test, but the explicit writer-to-reader contract is stale and would not catch accidental removal from the documented emitted labels.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Add `tiktok-paid` to WRITER_EMITS and keep a dedicated assertion that parseSource('tiktok-paid') round-trips as a known emitted source.

test_coverage_gaps.description: parseLineItems has no direct tests in the specified test file.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Malformed JSON, non-array JSON, non-string product IDs, empty product IDs, non-finite units/revenue, and whitespace normalization directly affect product-channel attribution when includeLineItems=true.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Call parseLineItems with valid `[{'p':' 123 ','u':2,'r':49.5}]` JSON, malformed JSON, object JSON, `{p:[1,2]}`, `{p:''}`, `{p:'123',u:'NaN',r:1}`, and assert only normalized valid items survive.
